review_candidates.title: Senior Systems Engineer, User Support
review_candidates.description: With a company culture rooted in collaboration, expertise and innovation, we aim to promote progress and inspire our clients, employees, investors and communities to achieve their greatest potential. Our work is the catalyst that helps others achieve their goals. In short, We Enable Possibility℠. The Senior Systems Engineer (Team Lead) is responsible for the administration and operation of the firm’s Infrastructure. This role requires an in-depth knowledge of Active Directory, Azure, MFA, VMware ESX, Windows security, and related technologies. The candidate will be part of the Cloud & Compute Engineering group. Candidate must be a self-starter, and demonstrate experience managing projects to completion. Candidate must be self-motivated, well organized and must have strong communications skills. This position works very closely with the Cloud, Compute and Messaging Engineering Teams and Senior Systems Engineers of IT Operations. Job Functions: Candidate MUST have strong Power Shell scripting experience as well as operational responsibility over the Active Directory, DNS, DHCP and PKI services. Strong Azure Iaas + PaaS and Office 365/Exchange Online experience. Install and maintain hardware and software on a virtualized Windows network. Develop processes and procedures to ensure managed environments maintain the highest levels of availability, security, and quality. Lead the security work stream of Active Directory consolidation program; Identify risks and provide guidance regarding remediation of gaps, to facilitate delivery of a hardened and sustainable AD environment. Deliver scripted solutions to assist with discovery and remediation of ad-hoc security gaps. Follow all set procedures and policies pertaining to the Change Management system. Develop capacity forecasts for managed environments that are proactive and prevent problems prior to outages. Manage "crisis situations" to a satisfactory conclusion (even under stress). Provide guidance on topics broadly related to information security risk and compliance. Serves as escalation point and provide troubleshooting guidance and direction in resolution of escalated issues and/or complex production, application or system problems. Candidate must be able to accommodate schedule flexibility to deal with escalations and occasional changes during non-core business hours. Required Skills A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience supporting a production environment. At least 3 to 5 years of relevant practical experience managing/troubleshooting authentication services. At least 5 plus years of strong Automation Experience.(PowerShell/Scripts/Terraform) At least 5 years of advanced level Active Directory experience. Knowledge of AKS, Kerberos, LDAP, Active Directory, DNS, DHCP. Experience with implementation of backup/restore and disaster and recovery strategies. Strong familiarity with security issues surrounding network computing and experience in implementation of security systems and controls. Strong knowledge of MFA, Enterprise Apps, IaaS and PaaS in MS Azure Expert knowledge of Active Directory, GPO's in a Windows Server 2019/2016 environment. Significant experience with Windows operating systems scripting and troubleshooting. Experience with user and security administration in the Windows environment. Extensive experience with maintenance and administration of VMWare virtualized systems. Knowledge of Microsoft Exchange, HP Proliant Servers, (Inc. iLO) are preferable. Knowledge of Microsoft Windows and Non-Windows Server architectures, Virtualization Technologies. Candidate must have a technologist mindset with aptitude to work on complex projects while possessing organization, time management, and multitasking skills. Candidates should have excellent written and oral communication skills with ability to cross-train team members. Strong ability to adapt to an extremely dynamic environment comprising of high degree of complexities and priorities. desirable Skills: Knowledge and experience of LAN/WAN/Firewall/VPN network technologies. Knowledge and experience of Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktop configuration and support in production environments. Knowledge and experience of Linux Knowledge and experience of Load Balancing technologies including configuration and support of production systems. Knowledge and experience of AWS Knowledge and experience of Cloud based security systems e.g. Tenable Nessus, Solarwinds, Mimecast, Crowdstrike Communication Skills: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including strong listening skills. Ability to effectively communicate business and technical information to audiences with varying backgrounds. Ability to communicate with offshore teams and technical development teams. Good documentation and presentation skills. Ability to interact with management in a professional manner. review_candidates.title: Systems Administrator
review_candidates.description: Darigold is seeking a highly skilled and motivated System Administrator to join our IT Operations team. The Systems Administrator provides support to and management of Darigold servers, storage, power, backup and recovery systems. Your expertise will ensure the smooth functioning, security and reliability of our critical IT systems, enabling our organization to operate efficiently and effectively. This role focuses on reliable execution, adherence to standards and collaboration within a security‑ and uptime‑critical environment. Darigold is the fifth largest dairy cooperative in the United States based on milk volume and one of the largest privately held organizations headquartered in the state of Washington. Since 1918, our producers have taken pride in producing dairy products with unsurpassed quality. Today, we are one of the nation's largest agricultural cooperatives, producing over 8.5 billion pounds of milk every year. Through innovative technology and our efficient, flexible production capabilities, we deliver value-added products and customer-driven solutions. Darigold is now known throughout the world for bringing fresh, wholesome dairy products and ingredients from the Northwest to people all around the globe. What You Will Do Infrastructure Management: Deploy, configure and maintain Dell server hardware, Dell Storage, Pure Storage arrays, APC UPS’s and other related infrastructure components, ensuring optimal performance and uptime. Hyper-V / VMware Virtualization: Manage and administer virtualization platforms, including cluster management, virtual machine deployment, resource allocation and performance tuning, to support efficient utilization of server resources and scalability. Windows Domain Services: Manage and administer Windows Domain Services, including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS and DHCP, File Servers and Exchange Hybrid. Backup and Recovery: Implement and oversee backup and recovery solutions to protect our data and ensure business continuity in case of any system failures or disasters. System Monitoring and Troubleshooting: Continuously monitor system performance, identify issues and promptly resolve technical problems to minimize downtime and disruptions. Patch and Update Management: Plan and execute regular software updates, security patches and firmware upgrades for the server and storage infrastructure. Capacity Planning: Assess and forecast system capacity requirements to anticipate future needs and recommend necessary upgrades or expansions. Documentation and Reporting: Maintain comprehensive documentation of IT systems, configurations, procedures and incidents. Generate regular reports on system performance, availability and security status. Collaboration and Support: Participate in required meetings, incident calls and remediation discussions, provide status updates and work collaboratively with team members, architects, security and vendors. Technical Validation: Validate configuration changes, assumptions and identified issues using documented standards, vendor documentation, system data or peer review before presenting findings or escalating concerns. Security Remediation & Hardening: Remediate vulnerabilities identified through penetration testing, audits and security assessments, including directory services, certificate services, virtualization platforms and management interfaces, in coordination with security and operations stakeholders. Technology Evaluation: Stay informed about the latest industry trends, best practices and advancements in server, storage and backup technologies identifying opportunities for improvement and supporting evaluation efforts to enhance the infrastructure’s efficiency and reliability. Work Prioritization & Execution: Execute assigned work according to defined priorities and timelines, including redirecting effort when priorities change due to incidents, security findings or business needs. On Call Support: Provide 24 x 7 On-Call support as part of a rotating schedule. Travel: Local and regional travel estimate of 25%. What You Will Bring Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or related field (or equivalent work experience). Minium of 5 years of proven experience as a System Administrator, preferably in a manufacturing or similar critical uptime environment. Knowledge of Dell server hardware, Dell Storage, Pure Storage and APC UPS systems. Experience with centrally managed virtualization environments, such as VMware vSphere or Microsoft System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM). Linux experience. Understanding of high-availability clustering concepts and experience in implementing and managing failover clustering solutions. Strong expertise in Windows Domain Services administration, including Active Directory, DNS and DHCP and File shares. Familiarity with backup and recovery solutions, such as Druva, Veeam, Commvault or similar platforms. Foundational knowledge of networking concepts to support on-call operations. Proficiency in PowerShell scripting for automating tasks, configuration management and system administration. Ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues independently and efficiently. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment. Demonstrated ability to follow technical direction, validate work before escalation and communicate issues clearly and professionally. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail. Relevant certifications (e.g., MCSE, CCNA, Dell EMC Proven Professional, Pure Storage Certified Administrator). IT experience in a manufacturing environment or other critical up-time environments such as medical, banking and utilities is a plus. Experience with NetBox, LogicMonitor, GitHub and PagerDuty is preferred. Benefits Of Working At Darigold We understand that as an employee, benefits that support you and your family in and out of work are important. We’re proud to offer eligible positions a competitive total rewards package that includes: 401k competitive employer matching Comprehensive medical, dental & vision benefits Employer paid life & disability coverage Paid time off and paid holidays 8 weeks paid parental leave Education assistance Employee assistance program Flexible hybrid working arrangement where it applies (up to 1 day/week after initial 90 days and approval by hiring manager and HR) Our Commitment To Diversity Achieving our vision to Lead Dairy Forward requires cultivating and supporting a team with varying backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are committed to providing a workplace based on mutual respect where all employees feel included and can bring their best and authentic selves to work every day. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and Affirmative Action Employer. We welcome all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability, marital status, creed, religion, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. As a condition of employment applicants offered a role will be required to successfully pass our pre-employment background screen, receive a negative drug screen result & confirm eligibility to work in the U.S. We participate in E-Verify - please follow the links for details, English / Spanish & view our Right to Work Statement, English / Spanish.

review_candidates.description: We are looking for a Network Engineer to work fully remotely for our client, a European institution based in Luxembourg. Architect and manage network security solutions, including firewalls, IDS/IPS, VPNs, and secure remote access. Perform threat hunting, vulnerability assessments, incident investigation, and root cause analysis. Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize network performance using tools such as Wireshark and tcpdump. Proven experience with cloud networking and security in AWS, Microsoft Azure, and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Strong knowledge of cybersecurity principles, threat detection, vulnerability management, and security monitoring. Experience with virtualization and infrastructure technologies such as VMware, Hyper-V, Proxmox, and Linux environments. Relevant certifications such as CCNP, Fortinet FCP/NSE, ISC2, or equivalent are highly desirable. This role supports secure enterprise technologies, network infrastructure, and operational IT systems essential to mission success. The selected candidate will assist with the installation, configuration, maintenance, and sustainment of enterprise hardware, software, servers, and network infrastructure across physical and virtual environments. The ideal candidate is a proactive technical professional capable of troubleshooting complex issues, supporting end users, and maintaining secure and reliable IT operations in fast-paced environments. Responsibilities include supporting Windows and Linux operating systems, VMware and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization platforms, and enterprise Microsoft services including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, DFS, SQL Server, and Azure. Additional duties include system monitoring, cybersecurity compliance support, backup and recovery operations, CAC authentication support, and troubleshooting hardware, software, network, and peripheral systems. The position also supports LAN connectivity, network cabling, switches, routers, printers, telephones, UPS systems, and Video Teleconference (VTC) systems, as well as IT equipment installation, relocation, accountability, sanitization, and disposal activities in accordance with DoD security policies and procedures. Key Responsibilities The Information Technology Specialist will Support IT systems, technical programs, projects, and operational tasks requiring advanced technical oversight and coordination Perform day-to-day IT operations to ensure system availability, performance, reliability, and compliance Coordinate with internal teams, customers, and stakeholders to ensure system requirements and project milestones are achieved Maintain and administer networked and standalone servers, workstations, user accounts, network access, security monitoring systems, and system documentation Analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve hardware, software, network, and system anomalies to maintain operational effectiveness Research, evaluate, and recommend system enhancements, emerging technologies, and IT solutions to improve mission performance Administer and support virtualized environments and enterprise services supporting mission operations Provide end-user and client technical support, including account provisioning, modification, and deactivation activities Identify Automated Information System (AIS) vulnerabilities and implement appropriate security countermeasures and remediation actions Ensure AIS and network infrastructure are operated, maintained, sanitized, and disposed of in accordance with applicable security policies and procedures Support Video Teleconference (VTC) systems, including scheduling, configuration, troubleshooting, and administration as required Skills And Experience The Information Technology Specialist must have Active Top-Secret clearance with eligibility for Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) access Minimum of 6 years of relevant Department of Defense (DoD) IT systems and operations experience Minimum of 2 years of experience supporting SAP and/or SCI environments within the past five (5) years Demonstrated experience supporting enterprise IT systems within secure, mission-critical environments Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capabilities across complex IT environments Experience supporting servers, workstations, virtualization platforms, network infrastructure, and enterprise services Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to leadership, customers, and non-technical stakeholders Proven ability to prioritize workloads, manage competing tasks, and operate independently with minimal supervision Education and Certifications The Information Technology Specialist must meet the following Required Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology (IT), or related discipline Security+, equivalent or higher to meet DoDM 8140.03 DCWF code 451 System Administrator-Intermediate Benefits Medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance Flexible Spending Accounts 401(k) PTO Paid Parental Leave Tuition reimbursement Paid federal holidays Security Clearance Must be a U.S. Citizen. A high-level Department of Defense active security clearance is/may be required. Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to government information. Physical Requirements Work may involve sitting or standing for extended periods of time and typing and reading from a computer screen. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About You And The Role You are joining Zipline as an Network Operations Field Support Engineer on our Network Operations team, supporting drone delivery and ground infrastructure that enable timecritical medical and commercial logistics. This is an owner‑level, frontline operations role: you will keep networked ground systems, fulfillment center connectivity, launch‑site communications, and site safety systems online across multiple operational sites. Your work directly affects mission availability, flight launch cadence, and customer deliveries; downtime delays flights and critical deliveries. You will operate in a mixed environment of office, warehouse, and outdoor launch sites; the role requires hands-on cabling and hardware work, real‑time incident response, and disciplined documentation. What You'll Do Own day-to-day monitoring and incident response for site and regional network infrastructure; respond to alerts, lead initial troubleshooting, and restore service within defined SLAs (example targets: initial response <15 minutes for P1, restore or escalate within 2 hours). Triage and resolve Tier 1/2 issues across LAN, WAN, VPN, DNS, DHCP, routing, switching, wireless, and site connectivity; validate fixes end-to-end and update tickets with root cause and remediation steps. Execute on-site hardware work: install, replace, cable, rack, label, and test switches, routers, wireless APs, servers, patch panels, UPS, and environmental sensors; perform structured cabling to ANSI/TIA-568.2-D standards. Lead outage playbook execution during maintenance windows and incident escalations; coordinate cross-functional handoffs with Flight Ops, Field Ops, Safety, and Network Engineering to minimize operational impact. Maintain and improve observability: operate monitoring and ticketing tools, and implement simple automations or monitoring thresholds to reduce repeat incidents and mean time to repair (MTTR). Drive continuous improvements by identifying recurring failure modes, proposing measurable fixes (e.g., reduce recurrence by X%, improve restore time by Y%), and partner with Network Engineering to implement changes. Provide on-call and shift coverage as scheduled, including occasional nights or weekend deployments to support launches and critical maintenance; travel regularly between regional sites (typical frequency: 25–50% depending on operational needs). What You'll Bring 1–3 years hands-on experience in network support, NOC operations, or field network engineering supporting production or business-critical systems; experience supporting operational sites or industrial environments is strongly preferred. Practical mastery of networking fundamentals: all layers of the OSI Model, TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, VLANs, switching, wireless, VPNs, and network troubleshooting methodologies. Hands-on structured cabling and hardware skills: running, terminating, testing, and labeling Cat5e/Cat6/Cat6a (shielded and unshielded) to ANSI/TIA standards; comfortable working in indoor racks and outdoor enclosures. Proven incident ownership: able to lead incident triage, runbooks, and post-incident documentation; evidence of reducing MTTR or ticket volume in previous roles is a plus. Comfortable operating under urgency and constrained conditions (field sites, weather, strict safety/aviation protocols); able to stay focused during outages and coordinate cross-functional stakeholders. Logistics and availability: able to travel between sites regularly (regional travel 25–50%), perform physical site work, and participate in scheduled on-call or shift rotations (including occasional nights/weekends). Tools/stack familiarity: experience with network monitoring and ticketing systems and basic command-line tools; experience with Linux, scripting (Python/Bash/PowerShell), or monitoring stacks is beneficial. Certifications or equivalent: CCNA, CompTIA Network+, military technical training, trade school credentials, or demonstrated hands-on experience in lieu of a degree. Hard constraints and operating expectations This role requires regular onsite work at operational centers and launch sites; remote-only candidates will not meet the role requirements. You must be able to perform physical site tasks (lifting equipment, climbing ladders, working in confined racks/ceilings) safely and reliably. What Else You Need To Know Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. review_candidates.title: Security Engineer
review_candidates.description: Why Seyfarth At Seyfarth, we understand that great people are the key to our success, and we provide the opportunities to match. If you join us, you’ll work with state-of-the-art technology in a friendly and professional environment, and we will continue to invest in your professional development. If you want the freedom to grow at a firm that is invested in your future, keep reading. The Opportunity As a Security Engineer - Application Security & Technology Risk , you will help evaluate and protect the Firm's technology environment by assessing the security risks associated with applications, SaaS platforms, browser extensions, integrations, and other technologies proposed for use within the Firm. A significant part of this role will involve understanding how a technology works, the access and permissions it requires, the data it can access or process, how it integrates with the Firm's environment, and how it could potentially be abused or compromised. You will evaluate these technologies from both a defensive and adversarial perspective, considering vulnerabilities, software supply-chain risk, authentication and authorization controls, configuration weaknesses, and the ways an attacker could leverage a compromised application or integration. The successful candidate will combine strong technical security knowledge with the ability to translate security findings into practical, risk-based recommendations for application owners, IT teams, and Firm leadership. The Day-To-Day On Any Given Day, You Will Work With Security, IT, Application Owners, Project Teams, Vendors, And Other Stakeholders On a Variety Of Technology Assessments And Security Initiatives. You Will Perform technical security assessments of software applications, SaaS platforms, browser extensions, integrations, AI-enabled technologies, and other technologies proposed for use within the Firm. Evaluate application architecture, permissions, data access, administrative controls, authentication methods, APIs, OAuth integrations, third-party dependencies, logging capabilities, and security configuration. Assess how compromised or malicious applications could be leveraged as an attack vector, including credential theft, data exposure, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, command and control, and software supply-chain compromise. Review vendor and application security documentation, vulnerability information, threat intelligence, software dependencies, and publicly available security research to identify potential risks. Evaluate authentication and authorization configurations including SSO, SAML, OAuth/OIDC, MFA, Microsoft Entra ID integrations, Conditional Access policies, service principals, application registrations, API permissions, and privileged access requirements. Work with infrastructure, endpoint, cloud, identity, networking, and application teams to identify security design or configuration gaps and recommend practical remediation or compensating controls. Review existing deployed applications to determine business need, usage, software versions, support status, known vulnerabilities, available updates, and potential security exposure. Assist with application inventory and software lifecycle initiatives designed to identify unnecessary, obsolete, vulnerable, or unauthorized applications within the environment. Validate approved application deployments to confirm that software, security controls, permissions, integrations, and configurations were implemented according to approved requirements. Use vulnerability management, endpoint security, SIEM, identity, network, asset discovery, and other security telemetry to understand application behavior and identify potential security concerns. Support Security Operations with threat hunting, security investigations, incident response, and other operational security activities as needed. Clearly document findings, risk, technical impact, and recommended controls for both technical and non-technical audiences. Exercise independent judgment, curiosity, and initiative when investigating unfamiliar technologies and security risks. You Have At least three years of experience in cybersecurity, security engineering, application security, vulnerability management, penetration testing, security operations, or a related technical information technology role. Strong understanding of common vulnerabilities, attack techniques, and the ways attackers compromise applications, endpoints, identities, cloud services, and enterprise environments. Strong understanding of software supply-chain risk, including compromised software updates, malicious dependencies, third-party libraries, browser extensions, package repositories, software signing, and vendor compromise. Familiarity with offensive security and penetration testing methodologies and the ability to apply an attacker mindset when evaluating new technologies. Experience evaluating applications or SaaS platforms from a security perspective, including permissions, architecture, integrations, authentication, authorization, data access, and administrative controls. Working knowledge of modern identity and authentication technologies including SSO, SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, MFA, Microsoft Entra ID, enterprise application registrations, and Conditional Access. Understanding of Windows and cloud security concepts, endpoint security controls, networking, APIs, and common enterprise application deployment models. Experience working with security technologies such as vulnerability scanners, endpoint detection and response platforms, SIEM platforms, identity security tools, network security platforms, or application security testing tools. Familiarity with tools such as Qualys, CrowdStrike Falcon, Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Entra ID, Burp Suite, or comparable security platforms is preferred. Ability to research unfamiliar technologies, understand how they operate, identify meaningful security concerns, and distinguish theoretical risk from realistic enterprise risk. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with attention to technical detail. Ability to communicate security findings clearly and work collaboratively with technical teams, application owners, vendors, and business stakeholders. Scripting, API, or automation experience with PowerShell, Python, or similar technologies is preferred. A strong desire to continuously learn about emerging technologies, vulnerabilities, attack techniques, and changes in the cyber threat landscape. What We Provide Seyfarth provides competitive salary and benefits at all levels, and our culture embraces the entrepreneurial spirit of its professionals like no other firm. Our professional staff are a collaborative team, helping to define the unique client experience offered by the firm. We understand that it takes more than attorneys to build a successful legal practice; everyone participates in our commitment to excellence. More About Seyfarth With approximately 1,000 lawyers across 19 offices, Seyfarth Shaw LLP provides advisory, litigation, and transactional legal services to clients worldwide. Learn more about The Seyfarth Experience at www.seyfarth.com/careers/. Seyfarth Shaw is committed to equal employment opportunity and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with physical and/or mental disabilities. We value and encourage diversity and solicit applications from all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, military and veteran status, gender identity or expression, genetic information, change of sex or transgender status, genetic information or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. This range is only applicable for jobs to be performed in Chicago. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s pay within the salary range will be based on numerous factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, experience, skills, and business or organizational needs. This job is also eligible for an annual merit increase and bonus pay. We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, and 401(k). We help organisations that rely on technology for critical operations, achieve and maintain a high-performance steady state. We have delivered projects for almost every police force and law enforcement agency in the UK, providing secure resilient networks and managed IT solutions. If you’re looking to develop your career in a high performing, dynamic team, where you can truly make a difference by delivering the technology that supports critical operations across the UK, this could be your ideal role. We are firm supporters of environmental, social and corporate governance and recognise that this is key to building a sustainable, investible business. The majority of staff work remotely with occasional office days, and we have systems in place to support employees to achieve their best work no matter their location. About the role The primary purpose is to build, sustain and continually improve an efficient, effective and profitable service desk delivering fast, reliable, friendly, proactive and expert 24x7 customer support. This role is based in the office of one of our most important customers, based in Central London and will require scheduled (and emergency) visits to other London based customers. Responsibilities will include: Working with the team to maintain a CSAT score of 8+ for all customers. Ensure 100% of new user requests are delivered on time and 100% of leaver requests are completed the day the user leaves. Acting as a technical point of escalation for service desk colleagues to help them resolve tickets the same day (preferably the same hour). review_candidates.title: Information Security Engineer
review_candidates.description: Join our growing team and discover why Summit Utilities, Inc. continues to earn national and regional recognition as an employer of choice. Our recognitions include Best Places to Work in Maine (2019–2025); Best Places to Work in Arkansas (2020, 2023, 2025); Best Places to Work in Oklahoma (2022–2025); Best Places to Work in Missouri (2023 and 2026); Best Places to Work in Colorado (2025); Forbes America’s Best Small Employers (2023); and, most recently, Proud and Purposeful Employer (2026). Summit is a growing natural gas utility providing safe, reliable, and clean burning natural gas service to homes and businesses in Arkansas, Colorado, Maine, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Texas. Being part of the Summit team means embracing excellence and innovation, committing to safety each and every day, and doing all that we can to serve each other, our customers, and the communities where we live. We aim to bring warmth and energy to everything we do. We have an exciting opportunity for an Information Security Engineer (SGL18). This role may be hybrid-based in Fort Smith or Little Rock, Arkansas. POSITION SUMMARY The Information Security Engineer is a hands-on technical specialist responsible for designing, building, and maintaining the security platforms, tooling, and automation that protect Summit Utilities' digital assets, operational technology, and data. This role owns the architecture and day-to-day engineering of core security capabilities — including SIEM, EDR, IAM, and cloud security posture management (CSPM) and builds the integrations and automation that let the broader security organization operate efficiently. The Information Security Engineer partners closely with the Information Security Architect, security operations, IT, and engineering teams to translate architecture standards and compliance requirements into working, production-grade security infrastructure. This role requires strong hands-on technical depth, coding and automation ability, and sound judgment in evaluating tooling and design trade-offs at scale. This position requires broad technical proficiency across security domains, strong engineering fundamentals, and the ability to communicate complex technical designs to both technical and non-technical audiences. PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Demonstrated experience designing, building, and operating security platforms (SIEM, EDR, IAM, CSPM) in production environments. Proven track record of building automation, integrations, or tooling that measurably reduced manual security work. Design, build, and maintain core security platforms — SIEM, EDR, IAM, and CSPM — including data pipelines, ingestion design, and platform integrations. Own the SIEM logging and detection data pipeline; design ingestion, parsing, and enrichment to support detection engineering and incident response. Build incident response tooling, forensic capabilities, and response automation to accelerate detection and response. Design and implement vulnerability scanning architecture and integrate vulnerability management into CI/CD pipelines. Build cloud security guardrails, infrastructure-as-code (IaC) security controls, and CSPM integrations across AWS, Azure, and/or GCP. Engineer the enterprise IAM platform, including identity federation, SSO, and automated provisioning/de-provisioning workflows. Architect and harden network and endpoint security controls (NGFW, EDR, segmentation) and evaluate emerging technologies. Build threat intelligence platform integrations and enrichment pipelines to support detection and response teams. Implement technical controls that satisfy compliance framework requirements (C2M2, NIST CSF, TSA Security Directives) in partnership with GRC. Provide technical evidence and configuration exports to support C2M2, NIST CSF, and TSA Security Directive audits and assessments. Support control testing by producing log samples, access reports, and system configuration artifacts requested by GRC/auditors. Document technical risk exceptions and compensating controls when a system can't fully meet a framework requirement. Maintain a mapping between deployed security tooling/controls and the specific framework requirements they satisfy. Design and deliver security platforms and integrations in alignment with enterprise reference architectures set by the Information Security Architect. Partner with engineering, platform, and product teams to embed secure design practices into the software delivery lifecycle. Serve as a technical mentor across the security organization; set and document engineering standards and best practices. Evaluate new security tools and technologies; drive build-vs-buy recommendations and proof-of-concept efforts. Participate in a shared on-call rotation to support critical security infrastructure and respond to platform-impacting issues.   POSITION QUALIFICATIONS EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Security, or a related field is required. Master's degree is preferred. 5–10+ years of progressive experience in security engineering or systems engineering. Professional certifications preferred: CISSP, GCIH, OSCP, AWS Certified Security – Specialty, Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer, or Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS). KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES  Hands-on expertise in operating and tuning SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel), including correlation rule and detection content development. Working knowledge of cloud security engineering across AWS, Azure, and/or GCP, including IaC security controls and CSPM tooling. Experience engineering identity and access management (IAM) platforms, federation/SSO, and privileged access management (PAM). Solid understanding of network and endpoint security technologies, including NGFW, EDR, and network segmentation. Experience integrating vulnerability management and security testing into CI/CD pipelines. Familiarity with threat intelligence platforms and enrichment pipeline design. Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (C2M2, NIST CSF, TSA Security Directives) and the ability to translate requirements into technical controls. Ability to evaluate tooling trade-offs, design integrations, and reason about scale, reliability, and operational impact. Strong communication skills; able to explain complex technical designs to both technical and non-technical audiences. Self-directed; able to drive multi-quarter engineering road maps with minimal supervision. Meticulous attention to detail when building, testing, and documenting security platforms and automation. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and/or skills required of all personnel so classified. Summit offers competitive pay and medical/dental/vision and other benefits that provide flexibility, choice, and support to our employees when they need it most. We understand that home and family are essential pieces of your life, and our benefits are designed to support you both at work and at home.  Summit Utilities, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability or veteran status.

You will work closely with our clients and internal teams to ensure timely and successful project completion. Key Responsibilities: 1. Own the integrated project management plan, approved scope, work breakdown structure, schedule, budget, resources, quality, procurement, communications, and acceptance baselines. 2. Lead requirements validation, site surveys, design coordination, interface management, constructability reviews, technical submittals, RFIs, and readiness planning with authorized reviewers. 3. Coordinate approved low-current/ELV systems and interfaces, including CCTV, access control, intercom, PA/BGM, AV, IPTV/SMATV, BMS/IBMS, parking/gates, nurse call and fire-alarm interfaces. 6. Manage technical procurement inputs, compliance matrices, BOQ reconciliation, long-lead items, vendor obligations, logistics, submittals and performance within delegated authority. 7. Maintain logic-linked schedules, evidence-based progress, cost forecasts, risk and issue registers, dependency controls, change requests, decision logs and recovery plans. 8. Plan controlled cutovers and migrations with impact assessment, prerequisites, approvals, communications, rollback triggers, command structure and post-change validation. 9. Lead inspection, testing, commissioning, defect closure and operational handover, including as-builts, configurations, certificates, licences, warranties, spares, training, asset/CMDB data, support contacts and residual-risk transfer. 10. review_candidates.description: About BlueHeart Energy BlueHeart Energy was founded in 2016 as a deep-tech company that has developed a new sustainable thermoacoustics technology to radically improve the performance of heat pumps, enabling them to evolve from being the best solution in the market to becoming the perfect solution. Our technology is a disruptive approach to generate heat and cold, with potential to revolutionize the whole industry. With our so called 'BlueHeart' engine, we turn heat pumps into affordable, silent and flexible devices, capable of working with wide temperature ranges suitable for both new and existing houses. Importantly, BlueHeart doesn’t require any refrigerants and doesn’t generate any CO2 emissions. The BlueHeart engine is also used for other (industrial) application to heat or cool. About the Role As Senior System Engineer (Thermoacoustic Heat Pump Systems) , you will support the development and integration of BlueHeart Energy's thermoacoustic heat pump technology by translating customer and product requirements into clear system specifications and engineering solutions. You will ensure that system requirements, interfaces, and performance targets are consistently implemented across the product and over the product lifecycle. You will collaborate closely with the Head of Development (who is also our system architect), and the Product and Component Owners to support the development of a reliable, efficient, and compliant heat pump system. In this role, you will drive the requirements management, verification and validation activities, configuration management and product baselining, support system integration (including interface definition and management), participate in technical trade-off analyses, and assist in identifying and mitigating technical risks, helping to ensure that subsystem developments align with overall system objectives. You promote systems thinking throughout the organization by challenging Product and Component Owners in system thinking, and you manage the evidence that the designed system satisfies stakeholder requirements throughout the product lifecycle. review_candidates.description: Company Profile CloudCIX Limited operates a data centre and cloud services hub from Hollyhill Industrial Estate in Cork, Ireland, under the business name Cork Internet eXchange (CIX). The company delivers a full vertical stack of services, including connectivity, colocation, public cloud (IaaS), HPC and AI/ML platforms (PaaS), and managed services. CloudCIX is also the developer of an open-source, multi-region, multi-tenant cloud computing platform used to support diverse infrastructure needs. Team members work in an environment that combines data centre operations with advanced cloud technologies. Applicants can learn more about the data centre and platform through the CloudCIX and CIX documentation and websites. Job Description Job Title: NOC Commander Salary: €36,000 per annum (€22.19 per hour worked/1,622 hours contracted per annum) Location: CloudCIX Limited, Hollyhill Industrial Estate, Cork T23 R68N (on-site) Probation Period: 6 months (performance review at conclusion). The first two months will be an intensive training period to transfer what we call the 'Fundamental Skillset'. Start Date: To be confirmed Duties and Responsibilities 1. 24/7 Monitoring & Incident Detection Monitor data centre infrastructure (servers, networking, storage, cloud services) using NOC tools e.g. Plot, Notes, Tester, Checker etc Detect and triage alerts (e.g., outages, performance degradation, security events) and fix, escalate to second support or to the NOC Operations Manager. Track SLA compliance (e.g., uptime, response times) and log all activities and duration in the ticketing system. 2. First-Line Incident Response Provide 'Remote Hands' services to customers and NOC 2nd Support Engineers. Follow documented procedures to restore service for common issues (e.g., server reboots, network port resets, service restarts). Escalate complex incidents (e.g., hardware failures, security breaches, DDoS attacks) to senior NOC staff or engineering teams. Assist in troubleshooting (e.g., checking logs, running diagnostics, verifying backups). 3. Security & Compliance Monitoring Monitor security alerts and flag suspicious activity to the NOC Operations Manager/CISO. Enforce security policies (e.g., access controls, patch management, vulnerability scans) in line with ISO 27001, PCI DSS, ISO 27017/27018. Verify compliance with data protection policies (e.g., GDPR, ISO 27018 PII handling). 4. Change & Configuration Management Execute approved changes (e.g., firmware updates, network reconfigurations) following change management procedures. Document all changes in the CMDB (Configuration Management Database). Assist in maintaining network diagrams, IP schemas, and asset inventories. 5. Customer & Internal Communication Provide timely updates to customers and internal teams during incidents (e.g., outages, maintenance). Log customer requests (e.g., port activations, firewall rule changes) and escalate to the appropriate team. Assist in security questionnaires (e.g., for ISO 27001/27017 compliance). 6. Performance & Capacity Monitoring Monitor system performance (CPU, memory, disk, network bandwidth) and report anomalies. Track capacity trends (e.g., storage, bandwidth) and flag potential issues to the NOC Commander Assist in cloud resource optimization (if applicable) to balance cost, performance, and security. 7. Documentation & Reporting Maintain accurate logs of all incidents, changes, and security events via the Ticketing System. Perform Quality Audits on Processes 8. Shift Handover & Team Collaboration Conduct thorough shift handovers (e.g., open tickets, ongoing incidents, pending changes). Assist colleagues during peak loads or complex incidents. Participate in training (e.g., security awareness, tool updates). If you are interested in this role, please send a CV to koc@cix.ie

review_candidates.title: ُElectricar Engineer Operations Manager – Water heating system
review_candidates.description: Company: BM Egypt Trade Department: After-Sales / Service Operations Reports To: General Manager / Board of Directors Location: Egypt Employment Type: Full-Time Industry: Home Appliances / Water Heating Systems Job Purpose The Operations Manager – After-Sales will be responsible for leading and managing the complete after-sales operation for BM Egypt Trade, with primary responsibility for instantaneous water heating systems , including installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, warranty, spare parts, field service, customer complaints, and technician performance. The role requires a qualified Engineer with strong technical knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems and proven experience managing service operations and field teams. The Operations Manager will ensure that all after-sales activities are delivered efficiently, safely, and within agreed service standards while maximizing customer satisfaction, controlling service costs, and protecting the company's brand reputation. Key Responsibilities1. After-Sales Operations Management Manage the complete daily operation of the After-Sales Department. Develop and implement service procedures, workflows, and operating standards. Ensure all customer service requests are registered, assigned, followed up, and closed within agreed timelines. Monitor the complete service cycle from customer complaint through technician visit, diagnosis, repair, testing, and closure. Ensure proper coordination between Customer Service, Call Center, Sales, Warehouse, Accounting, and After-Sales. Establish clear escalation procedures for critical technical and customer complaints. Ensure all open service orders are continuously followed up until final closure. 2. Technical Management – Instant Water Heaters Lead the technical operation related to instantaneous water heating systems . Supervise installation, commissioning, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair activities. Ensure correct diagnosis of electrical, electronic, hydraulic, heating, and control-system failures. Review recurring technical failures and identify root causes. Develop technical solutions to reduce repeat complaints and unnecessary replacements. Ensure technicians follow manufacturer specifications and approved technical procedures. Review difficult or escalated technical cases personally when required. Support the team in diagnosing complex failures involving heating elements, sensors, flow systems, control boards, electrical protection, water pressure, and temperature regulation. Instant water heaters require particular attention to electrical safety, water flow, protection systems, and correct installation; the role should therefore maintain strict technical and safety controls. 3. Installation & Commissioning Establish and monitor installation standards for instant water heaters. Ensure installations are performed by properly trained and qualified technicians. Verify correct electrical connections, water connections, pressure, flow, safety devices, and operational testing. Ensure every installation is properly tested before customer handover. Monitor installation quality and repeat installation complaints. Develop installation checklists and technical inspection procedures. Conduct random quality audits on completed installations. 4. Maintenance & Technical Service Develop preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Ensure technicians perform repairs according to approved technical procedures. Monitor first-time-fix rate and repeat visits. Reduce unnecessary part replacement and technical misdiagnosis. Ensure proper testing of repaired units before closing service orders. Establish technical escalation procedures for unresolved problems. Monitor product failure trends and provide technical recommendations to management. 5. Warranty Management Manage the complete warranty process. Establish clear criteria for warranty acceptance and rejection. Control warranty costs and unnecessary replacements. Review warranty claims and identify recurring product issues. Coordinate with suppliers/manufacturers regarding technical issues and warranty claims. Ensure proper documentation for all warranty cases. Monitor warranty cost as a percentage of sales. 6. Spare Parts Management Coordinate with Warehouse and Procurement to ensure availability of critical spare parts. Establish minimum and maximum stock levels for fast-moving service parts. Monitor spare-parts consumption by product and failure type. Reduce unnecessary parts usage and unexplained inventory discrepancies. Identify obsolete and slow-moving service parts. Ensure technicians properly document all parts used on each service order. 7. Technician & Team Management Manage, supervise, and develop the technical service team. Set clear responsibilities and performance expectations for technicians and supervisors. Monitor daily technician productivity and field performance. Evaluate technician technical skills and identify training requirements. Establish technician performance KPIs. Conduct regular performance reviews. Ensure proper attendance, discipline, uniform, tools, and professional customer behavior. Develop a technical skills matrix for all technicians. Ensure technicians are adequately trained before handling products independently. 8. Customer Experience Ensure professional handling of customer complaints and escalations. Monitor customer satisfaction after service completion. Analyze customer complaints to identify operational and technical weaknesses. Establish procedures for VIP and high-priority customers. Ensure customers receive accurate information regarding appointment times, diagnosis, repair, warranty, and expected completion. Reduce customer waiting time and repeat complaints. 9. Service Network Management Develop and manage authorized service providers and external technicians when required. Evaluate service providers based on quality, response time, technical capability, and customer satisfaction. Establish service-level agreements and performance requirements. Conduct periodic audits of service providers. Develop backup service coverage for key geographic areas. Required Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Engineering is mandatory. Preferred majors: Mechanical Engineering Electrical Engineering Mechatronics Engineering Electromechanical Engineering 5–8 years of relevant experience , preferably within: Water heaters Home appliances HVAC Electrical appliances Technical service After-sales operations Minimum 3 years in a supervisory/managerial after-sales or service role . Strong practical knowledge of electrical and mechanical troubleshooting. Experience with installation and maintenance operations. Experience managing technicians and field-service teams. Strong understanding of warranty and spare-parts operations. Good knowledge of technical drawings, wiring diagrams, and service manuals. Excellent Excel skills and ability to analyze operational KPIs. ERP/service-management-system experience is preferred. Very good English communication skills. Engineering degrees and technical experience are particularly appropriate for after-sales roles involving water-heating equipment because service work combines technical troubleshooting, installation, maintenance, safety, and customer-facing operations. Technical Competencies The candidate should have strong knowledge of: Instantaneous water heaters. Electrical heating systems. Heating elements. Thermostats and temperature sensors. Flow sensors/switches. Water pressure and flow requirements. Electrical protection systems. Control boards and electronic components. Wiring and electrical diagrams. Hydraulic connections. Leakage diagnosis. Overheating protection. Preventive maintenance. Fault diagnosis and root-cause analysis. Product installation and commissioning. Warranty assessment. Leadership Competencies Strong leadership and team-management skills. Excellent problem-solving ability. Decision-making under pressure. Customer-oriented mindset. Strong operational discipline. Ability to manage multiple field teams simultaneously. Strong negotiation and communication skills. Analytical thinking. Ability to establish and enforce procedures. Ability to hold teams accountable for performance. High level of ownership and responsibility. Authority & Decision-Making The Operations Manager will have authority to: Assign and redistribute service orders. Escalate technical cases. Approve service actions within approved company limits. Recommend warranty approvals/rejections. Recommend technician disciplinary actions based on company policy. Recommend spare-parts purchases. Recommend replacement of defective products. Evaluate and recommend service providers. Recommend recruitment, training, promotion, or replacement of technical staff.

review_candidates.title: Manager, Supplier Relationships
review_candidates.description: Primary Work Address: 4000 Jones Bridge Road, Chevy Chase, MD, 20815 Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account. HHMI is focused on supporting and moving science forward in a variety of different ways ranging from conducting basic biomedical research, empowering educators, inspiring students, developing the next generation of scientists – even stretching into film and media production. Our Headquarters is in the greater Washington, DC metro area and is home to over 300 employees with expertise in investments, communications, digital production, biomedical sciences, and everything in between. The work housed here supports and augments the groundbreaking research conducted in HHMI labs across the nation. As HHMI scientists continue to push boundaries in laboratories and classrooms, you can be sure that your contributions while working here are making a difference. This is a role for someone who treats a supplier relationship as a long game, not a transaction to close and forget. The Manager, Supplier Relationships sits inside HHMI's Procurement team, supporting every lab and administrative group across the Institute. Whoever needs a supplier vetted, a contract negotiated, or an escalated problem resolved gets the same level of support, whether they sit at Headquarters or in a lab three time zones away. Procurement at HHMI runs at real scale, and the tools available to do it well, including AI-assisted contract review and spend analysis, are moving fast. This role is expected to keep pace with them and bring the rest of the sourcing team along. The role runs the full sourcing cycle: researching the market, issuing RFPs, collaborating with the Office of General Counsel (OGC) to negotiate contracts, and managing the relationship after signature, using AI throughout to move faster while relying on sound judgment for the calls that matter. It also involves directing a team, translating procurement strategy into day-to-day work, and giving people the kind of feedback that actually changes how they perform. This position works on a hybrid schedule, reporting in-person three days a week to our headquarters in Chevy Chase, Maryland. How to Apply Interested candidates are encouraged to submit a resume along with a cover letter describing their interest in this role and how their experience aligns with it. We encourage qualified candidates who are eligible to work in the United States to apply. Please note, we are not able to sponsor a visa for this position at this time. What You Will Actually Do Own the sourcing cycle. Lead market research, RFP development, and supplier selection from open to close, using AI tools to speed up the process and sound judgment to close it out. Set the AI agenda. Work with procurement leadership to decide how AI fits into sourcing and supplier management, and keep the team’s AI priorities aligned with where the Institute is headed. Negotiate and manage contracts. Negotiate pricing, service levels, and terms; manage renewals; and run regular supplier performance and risk evaluations. Direct the sourcing team. Assign work, hold it to productivity, efficiency, and accuracy targets, and coach a small team through the decisions they face day to day. Coordinate the supplier lifecycle. Manage requests to add, change, or retire suppliers, and set up the administrative and catalog support that keeps ordering running once a contract is signed. Partner across the Institute. Work with the OGC to keep competitive sourcing fair, ethical, and consistent, and with purchasing leadership and stakeholders to turn business needs into procurement requirements. Read the data and act on it. Track spend, benchmark cost, and calculate ROI on sourcing decisions, using AI to speed up the analysis and sound judgment to decide what it means. Keep the process current. Review procurement policies, RFP templates, and due diligence questionnaires on a regular cycle, and update them as the work and the tools change. What We Are Looking For A negotiator's instinct. Knowing what a strong SLA looks like versus a weak one, and how to walk into a renewal with leverage instead of hope. AI alongside judgment, not instead of it. Comfortable using AI tools to speed up contract review, spend analysis, and supplier research, and knowing when to trust the output and when to check it yourself before it goes external. A real coaching habit. Able direct a team's work, give feedback that changes behavior, and hold people to a standard without micromanaging them. Institutional fluency. Eight or more years in procurement, ideally somewhere with the complexity of an academic or research institution, developing the ability to move a sourcing decision through OGC and stakeholders without losing the thread. Hard conversations, done well. Able to hold a supplier accountable in a difficult conversation, or push back on an internal stakeholder's ask, without burning the relationship. Fluent in the numbers. Cost analysis, spend benchmarking, and ROI calculations are part of how this person thinks through a sourcing decision, not an afterthought handed off to someone else. Nice to have Experience with contract management software beyond core Microsoft Office tools. Exposure to sourcing or procurement in a research or academic setting. What This Role Is Not A role where AI makes the call. AI is used throughout sourcing, contracting, and spend analysis, but the decisions on pricing, risk , and supplier wins remain owned by the Manager, Supplier Relationships. A purely tactical buying role. This is not just processing purchase orders. It is setting sourcing strategy, running RFPs, and sitting at the negotiating table. A role you run solo. Every competitive sourcing process here moves through the OGC and depends on stakeholders across the institute. This role keeps that coordination moving, rather than working in isolation. Practical details This role is based at HHMI Headquarters and reports to the Director, Procurement. It requires a bachelor's degree , CPM, CPSM, or CPIM certification, and eight or more years of progressively responsible procurement experience, preferably in an academic or research environment. Physical Requirements Remaining in a normal seated or standing position for extended periods of time; reaching and grasping by extending hand(s) or arm(s); dexterity to manipulate objects with fingers, for example using a keyboard; communication skills using the spoken word; ability to see and hear within normal parameters; ability to move about workspace. The position requires mobility, including the ability to move materials weighing up to several pounds (such as a laptop computer or tablet). Persons with disabilities may be able to perform the essential duties of this position with reasonable accommodation. Requests for reasonable accommodation will be evaluated on an individual basis. Please Note This job description sets forth the job’s principal duties, responsibilities, and requirements; it should not be construed as an exhaustive statement, however. Unless they begin with the word “may,” the Essential Duties and Responsibilities described above are “essential functions” of the job, as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act. Compensation And Benefits Our employees are compensated from a total rewards perspective in many ways for their contributions to our mission, including competitive pay, exceptional health benefits, retirement plans, time off, and a range of recognition and wellness programs. Visit our Benefits at HHMI site to learn more. Hiring Pay Range $121,823.94 - $152,279.92 Pay Type: Annual The posted range reflects HHMI’s good faith estimate of the anticipated hiring salary range for this role at the time of posting. Actual hiring compensation is determined by a candidate’s qualifications, experience, and internal equity. HHMI is an Equal Opportunity Employer We use E-Verify to confirm the identity and employment eligibility of all new hires.

Maintain and monitor data pipelines, resolving any failures or inefficiencies. Implement automated CI/CD pipelines for data workflows. Design and implement data ingestion pipelines from ERP systems (Oracle EBS / Fusion/ NetSuite), REST APIs and external data sources. Handle API pagination and rate limits, schema changes and evolving data structures. Implement incremental data loading strategies using timestamps, change tracking, CDC (where applicable) Work with existing platforms such as Google BigQuery during transition phase. 3. Lakehouse Architecture & Data Structuring Design and maintain Bronze / Silver / Gold layers. Ensure data is clean, standardized, analytics ready. Structure data to support downstream semantic models and reporting. 4. Data Security and Compliance Implement best practices for data security, ensuring compliance with regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, and company policies. Work with cybersecurity teams to safeguard sensitive data from unauthorized access. Ensure proper data backup and disaster recovery strategies are in place. 5. Collaboration with Business and IT Teams Work closely with data analysts, analytics engineers, IT teams and business stakeholders to understand data requirements. Provide technical expertise and recommendations for data processing and storage solutions. 6. Data Performance and Optimization Continuously optimize data pipelines for performance, scalability, and cost efficiency. Troubleshoot and resolve data-related performance issues in databases and processing workflows. Optimize query performance for data retrieval and reporting needs. 7. Data Governance and Quality Ensure high data quality by implementing validation and cleansing techniques. Develop data monitoring processes to track data accuracy and completeness. Work with data architects to align data engineering solutions with governance policies. 8. Documentation and Reporting Document data pipeline structures, workflows, and integrations for future reference. Provide reports and insights on data pipeline performance and efficiency. 9. Stay Updated on Technology Trends Stay current with advancements in data engineering, AI, cloud computing, and big data technologies. Evaluate and integrate new tools and techniques to improve data processing. 10. Support Data Analytics and Business Intelligence Provide clean, structured, and accessible data for analysts and data scientists. Work with BI teams to ensure that data warehouses and reporting tools function efficiently. Qualifications: Education Required: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, or a related field. Master's degree and/or cloud certifications (Azure Solutions Architect, Azure Data Engineer, Azure AI Engineer, Databricks) are a plus. Field of Experience: Data Engineering: Hands-on experience in building and managing data pipelines and workflows. Database Management: Experience working with relational and NoSQL databases. Data Integration: Proficiency in integrating multiple data sources and managing data transformations. Experience implementing CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps) Cloud Computing: Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Big Data Processing: Understanding of distributed data processing frameworks and tools. Years of Experience: Typically, 3 to 7 years of experience in data engineering or a related IT field. At least 3 years of hands-on experience in data pipeline development, ETL processes, and working with cloud-based data solutions. Technical Skills: Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Fabric on Azure Strong understanding of Microsoft Fabric architecture including OneLake Strong proficiency in SQL and Python for data processing Proficiency in Apache Spark (PySpark preferred) Strong understanding of medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold layers) Proven experience in building metadata-driven data pipelines Experience with ETL/ELT design and optimization Knowledge of Azure ecosystem and integration patterns Strong understanding of data governance, lineage, and compliance

Darigold is the fifth largest dairy cooperative in the United States based on milk volume and one of the largest privately held organizations headquartered in the state of Washington. Since 1918, our producers have taken pride in producing dairy products with unsurpassed quality. Today, we are one of the nation's largest agricultural cooperatives, producing over 8.5 billion pounds of milk every year. Patch and Update Management: Plan and execute regular software updates, security patches and firmware upgrades for the server and storage infrastructure. Capacity Planning: Assess and forecast system capacity requirements to anticipate future needs and recommend necessary upgrades or expansions. Documentation and Reporting: Maintain comprehensive documentation of IT systems, configurations, procedures and incidents. Collaboration and Support: Participate in required meetings, incident calls and remediation discussions, provide status updates and work collaboratively with team members, architects, security and vendors. Technical Validation: Validate configuration changes, assumptions and identified issues using documented standards, vendor documentation, system data or peer review before presenting findings or escalating concerns. Security Remediation & Hardening: Remediate vulnerabilities identified through penetration testing, audits and security assessments, including directory services, certificate services, virtualization platforms and management interfaces, in coordination with security and operations stakeholders. Technology Evaluation: Stay informed about the latest industry trends, best practices and advancements in server, storage and backup technologies identifying opportunities for improvement and supporting evaluation efforts to enhance the infrastructure’s efficiency and reliability. Work Prioritization & Execution: Execute assigned work according to defined priorities and timelines, including redirecting effort when priorities change due to incidents, security findings or business needs. Minium of 5 years of proven experience as a System Administrator, preferably in a manufacturing or similar critical uptime environment. Knowledge of Dell server hardware, Dell Storage, Pure Storage and APC UPS systems. Understanding of high-availability clustering concepts and experience in implementing and managing failover clustering solutions. Strong expertise in Windows Domain Services administration, including Active Directory, DNS and DHCP and File shares. Familiarity with backup and recovery solutions, such as Druva, Veeam, Commvault or similar platforms. Foundational knowledge of networking concepts to support on-call operations. Proficiency in PowerShell scripting for automating tasks, configuration management and system administration. Ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues independently and efficiently. Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment. Demonstrated ability to follow technical direction, validate work before escalation and communicate issues clearly and professionally. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail. Relevant certifications (e.g., MCSE, CCNA, Dell EMC Proven Professional, Pure Storage Certified Administrator). IT experience in a manufacturing environment or other critical up-time environments such as medical, banking and utilities is a plus. Experience with NetBox, LogicMonitor, GitHub and PagerDuty is preferred.
